personal.text:
I was invited here for a work-related/industry-related dinner. I wouldn't usually have accepted the invite so quickly, but I'd read about Abaca when it opened, and had walked past it, but hadn't found the occasion to try it yet. What luck! 

The VC who helped organize the event loves Abaca, and has had them cater multiple events. 

Our group tried 
- Seafood pancit: handmade noodles, XO bagoong, king trumpet mushrooms. Delicious,  and I don't even like mushrooms usually. Loved the noodle texture and flavor, the variety of seafood, and the depth of the combination of ingredients. 
- Thin cut pork skewers, organic hodo soy yuba skin skewers. Seemingly-simple, yet more satisfying than your typical skewers.
- Grilled market vegetables with coconut sauce--perfectly grilled, these vegetables would appease anyone who is not a vegetable fan (as well as your typical veggie fan.)
- Lechon pork belly with tomato sarsa--I'd never heard of "lechon" before, but upon further research after trying it, I learned it is a Spanish word for a roasted piglet which was still fed by suckling its mother's milk (a suckling pig). Lechón is a popular food in Spanish-speaking nations. Delicious! Hefty pieces, I wish they'd come cut already.
- Whole petrole sole, double fried with sinigang glaze. Difficult to get the fish, very good fried. 
- Pork steamed bun: bacon tocino marinated, black garlic, pineapple kimchi. Not your typical bun! I'm honestly surprised the black garlic made the bun turn so black. Tocino means bacon in Spanish, usually made from the pork belly. Thick and messy, this bun-lover had two!
- Cocktail with pandan-so good! I wish I'd had one of the ube cocktails as well. 
- Pandan bibingka dessert. Best dessert. The table kept talking about this dish.
- Chocolate mousse dessert. Good, not a standout dish.

I loved the atmosphere and the staff was so attentive. They made special dishes upon learning of different customers' allergies. They helped package up to-go containers, moved dishes around the large table so everyone could try some, and were friendly and funny!

I can't wait to come back with friends and family to see what Abaca does next, and I look forward to being able to say I was a fan of them before they got their first Michelin star! (I predict this will happen.)

personal.text:
Inevitably just by spending some time in San Francisco you will have heard of the beauty that is Burma Superstar, one of my favorite restaurants in San Francisco.

Be prepared to wait 1+ hours but it'll be worth it for the complex flavors waiting for you. 

The menu is pretty large so you have lots of options, so I recommend going with a group so you can try more. In my experience with a group of three, you really can't go wrong with any dish. 

We started off with the Platha and Dip and ended with the Black rice pudding. I think you can pass on the pudding but the Platha was warm and crispy. 

Our main dishes were the Chili Lamb, Fiery Pork, and Sesame Chicken. Each one was cooked and seasoned well but my favorite was the Chili Lamb. They all came with some vegetables but not many, and had slightly different spices. 

My main gripe was that the size of a serving of Coconut Rice is very small--maybe I'm used to family-style Chinese cuisine, but I expected more rice with each bite of meat. 

Also would recommend the I Know Kung Fu Soju. They have a rather large drink menu as well. 

TLDR seeking some high-quality excitement and spice? Come here!

personal.text:
I've been meaning to come here for a while since I read about Cafe de Olla in Mission Local pre-pandemic.

"Café de Olla"  literally means "coffee from the pot" and is a significant drink of Mexico. I love that it's community-oriented. It doesn't feel like most coffee shops in SF and prices are very reasonable and accessible. 

I enjoyed my mate latte and pan dulce while writing (free wifi! Cute tables and art!) Will be back to try tamales, quesadillas, and other dishes and drinks.  

Love the owners Eduardo and Francisco who are friends who met through a LGBTQ group. Service is immaculate!

personal.text:
My family and I came here with a large group after we watched the Odyssey at the Metreon. It wasn't a long walk to get here! 

They have a pretty good happy hour if that's up your alley. 

I enjoyed my Dandan noodles. They were filling and had a nice portion of vegetables. I liked the sauce flavor. Others enjoyed the chicken katsu sandwich. 

We also shared salt and pepper calamari, buns, butternut squash dumplings, oysters, and buns for appetizers. My favorites were the butternut squash dumplings (so unique! So fresh! So fun.) and the oysters (good flavor.)

For cocktails and drinks, I liked the Kimchi Bloody Mary and a friend enjoyed the Pea flower cocktail. I love a Bloody Mary and this was a good one. Fresh tomato flavor and not too much vodka (hey, I'm a light-weight!)

Service was attentive and wonderful. Bathrooms are clean. Decor is fun and homey.

Service was very good. Love the outdoor parklet and sidewalk tables. Will be back.

personal.text:
Make a reservation here for a Wednesday night or you may not get seated! It was packed! Lots of recent college grads--some of them I thought looked like they could be in high school.

We were seated in a parklet outside and the heat lamp was not on, but it was on in the other one because that one had more people!

The chips and guac were pricey ($13ish) but very good. 

My boyfriend and I enjoyed carne asada and carnitas fajitas. Both were filling, flavorful, and juicy. The cocktails and margaritas are also very good! Will be back.

personal.text:
There's not many restaurants I'd walk through this seedy part of the Tenderloin for, but the great Thai food at Lers Ros makes it one of them. 

We had a reservation for a Thursday night around 6 but ended up not needing it? It wasn't very packed at the time, but it's always good to be on the safe side.

Two friends and I went family-style again and shared barbecue pork, pad see-ew, garlic quail, and I had the Thai iced tea as well. My favorite dishes were either the barbecue pork or the quail. The pork was crisp, chewy, and full of flavor. 

A friend had heard good things about the pad see-ew, but we thought it was just okay. 

Service is quick and bathroom is clean. Would be back.

personal.text:
Love the burgers and steaks. Prices are high but they give you a lot of food and it's top-quality in an upscale setting and location (the bottom of a Nob Hill condominium next to the Masonic, so it's good to see a show at.)

Fries are very good and steaks are juicy. Best burger in SF IMO and it's 2 meals!

I love the art deco theme. There's an excellent happy hour at the bar or in the lounge from 5-6pm daily. $8 cocktails and drinks and also steak frites or sandwich for under $30! 

Service is excellent. I love Eddie and Riley at the bar! I come back and I bring friends. More people should go to Osso for date night, special occasions, a night cap, before or after shows, or just because!

personal.text:
It took me a while to make it out to Palette Tea House, and they did not disappoint! 

My friend Kimberly made a reservation for 2 one Sunday early afternoon (not many open reservations were available!) and when we got there, their outdoor (and indoor) dining was packed! It took a few minutes to get seated even though we had a reservation. No biggie, it was worth it!

Plates were in the style of PALETTES hence the name. We shared Salted Egg Lava Bao, Palette Soup Dumplings (XLB), Premium Scallop Siu Mai, Black Swan Taro Puff, and I had Boozy Milk tea while she had the Strawberry Mimosa. Yes, it was all Instagrammable, but it was also very unique. This is not typical dim sum--Palette puts their own spin on everything, making for a fun, worthwhile trip and experience. Besides having great food, expect great views, great outdoor seating (and indoor), great decor, and service was impeccable as well!
